transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-15
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~65 mins
Attendees: Maya, Diego, Sasha, Anika, Owen, Riley

[00:00] Maya: okay let's get started, thanks everyone for joining, we have a pretty full agenda, this is the greenfield kernel rollout preflight, uh, objective is to confirm canary gating, verify mitigations from the last OOM, and greenlight the dry run next week
[00:15] Diego: quick note — this is targeted for next monday for canary 1, then a wider push on thursday if all good, timeline's tight so we need to be pragmatic on gates
[00:30] Sasha: yeah, and we still have the residual from the gpu oom incident two weeks ago — heap fragmentation + scheduler backpressure, so we've got to validate the kernel fallback path thoroughly
[00:45] Owen: a couple items from runtime — the new kernel has an optimistic memory allocator that reduces peak by about 12% in our internal bench, but switches to a fallback kernel when a high-water mark is hit. The fallback has slightly higher latency but avoids OOMs.
[01:10] Riley: when you say "fallback" can you clarify? is it an alternate kernel binary or a config toggle?
[01:20] Owen: it's binary-level fallback, we maintain two kernel builds shipped in same image. We flip a runtime flag when mem pressure exceeds threshold. The problem we saw is the flip was too late under sudden spike.
[01:36] Anika: so the release plan needs to include a canary traffic pattern that simulates the sudden spike scenario — not just steady-state throughput
[01:48] Maya: agreed — Diego can you confirm canary phases?
[01:52] Diego: phase 0: internal canary (10% traffic) for 6 hours, phase 1: staggered gradual increase to 30% over 3 hours, with a deliberate spiky run in the middle. We will hold if latency  p99 > target or error rate increases 2x baseline
[02:12] Sasha: we need clearer triggers: what exact metrics, and what windows. For example p99 over 5m > 280ms, or kernel fallback count > 5 per minute should trigger auto-rollback
[02:30] Owen: we can emit a telemetry event on fallback switch, it's fairly cheap to add a counter to prometheus, I'll add histograms for switch latency too
[02:45] Riley: QA will need those events to build failure injections into smoke tests — can we get a test hook?
[02:53] Owen: yes, we have a test env flag that forces fallback. I'll document the CLI toggle in the release playbook
[03:10] Maya: point on SLOs — are we comfortable with the rollback thresholds Sasha suggested?
[03:18] Sasha: they're conservative; main concern is false positives during noisy minute windows so we should use sustained windows like a 5m median and a 1m spike threshold combined
[03:30] Diego: also want to ensure the scheduler backpressure mitigation is in place — last time the scheduler starved smaller-batch requests while trying to salvage large ones
[03:40] Owen: that's due to our continuous batching heuristics — the new heuristic includes a per-tenant max-batch-size cap and a soft-preemption signal, but it wasn't live-tested at scale
[03:55] Anika: so action item to run a simulated tenant mix with small and large requests; we should mirror production percentiles for seq length and batch sizes
[04:06] Riley: QA will prepare the tenant-mix matrix, seems like a crucial test for the dry-run
[04:15] Maya: good. Next — postmortem follow-ups from the OOM. Diego, you were driving the incident review — what's outstanding?
[04:26] Diego: root cause was a combination: kernel memory accounting drift under specific long-sequence workloads and a bug in the preemption threshold. We mitigated with a hotfix but need a permanent fix and an e2e perf run across the corpus. Also need better auto-triage logs in the incident runbook
[04:50] Sasha: I still want an audit of KMS usage in the private clusters — during the incident we couldn't quickly verify key rotation state, that slowed down recovery by about 14 minutes
[05:02] Anika: noted — I'll add KMS checks to the checklist, plus exact commands to verify key status; we should also add a pointer to the audit logs
[05:15] Owen: related note: the KV cache telemetry is sparse for longer sequences, we should add a time-series for prefix cache hit rate by sequence length bucket, it's important for the new kernel's memory profile
[05:30] Riley: QA observed a regression in throughput for the long-seq test in the nightly after the new kernel landed, about 4% worse median but 10% better p95 — mixed signal, need deeper analysis
[05:46] Diego: that could be quantization path interacting with kernel code, might be in the compilation/kernelselect logic, Owen can you take that?
[05:55] Owen: yep I'll run the compile matrix and sanity check the quant path toggles, and include microbench numbers
[06:10] Maya: anything blocking from release engineering? Anika?
[06:15] Anika: packaging is done; the image includes both kernel variants, but we need a final e2e verification: smoke, canary, rollback, and post-rollback cleanup test. Also want the dry-run choreography doc approved by product & SRE
[06:30] Sasha: SRE will run the simulated spike and confirm telemetry flows; also we'll run an automated rollback using the playbook to make sure it's scripted end-to-end, not manual steps hidden in someone's head
[06:44] Riley: for QA sign off we need a matrix: smoke passes, soak for 2 hours at 10% traffic, spike experiment, rollback test. We'll attach logs and a pass/fail checklist to the release doc
[06:58] Diego: timeline recap — we want final artifacts by wednesday: perf runs, updated runbook, and the playbook. Dry-run on tuesday next week, final canary on thursday. Does that still work?
[07:10] Maya: yes, but add contingency — if any perf run shows regression >5% median or p95 worse by 10% we halt and call an emergency patch window
[07:22] Owen: quick technical question — when fallback triggers, do we preserve KV cache state or drop it? Current behavior is preserve but rehydrate lazily which caused spike in IO
[07:32] Anika: preserving is preferable for quality but we need to avoid IO storms; maybe add a staged rehydrate with jitter
[07:40] Sasha: we'll test staged rehydrate in the canary env and have IO threshold alarms so we can auto-throttle rehydration if underlying disk is saturated
[07:52] Riley: also want smoke tests to check for repeated fallback loops — e g fallback->rehydrate->fallback — ensure there's a loop-breaker counter in the runtime
[08:05] Owen: good call, I'll add a backoff counter and emit a loop-break event when exceeded
[08:18] Maya: communications — we need a short Ops bulletin for customer-facing teams describing expected behavior during canary and advisory language in case visible latencies rise transiently
[08:30] Diego: I'll draft the bulletin, include expected SLOs and recommended customer messaging, and coordinate with support to open a watch channel during the canary window
[08:42] Anika: on release packaging, I also want to include checksums and provenance metadata in the artifact so we can quickly verify image contents in customer clusters
[08:55] Sasha: security note — ensure the image build signs are present and the SBOM is attached in the release page, add KMS key id for the signing key
[09:06] Maya: perfect. let's go around for quick confirmations and owners
[09:10] Diego: I'll own the perf runs and the postmortem closeout
[09:14] Owen: I'll add the telemetry counters and test hooks plus the fallback loop-breaker
[09:18] Sasha: SRE will run the spike sim and validate rollback automation
[09:22] Anika: Release will author the playbook and packaging checks, and run the dry-run choreography
[09:26] Riley: QA will complete the smoke/soak matrix and sign off on test artifacts
[09:30] Maya: I'll collate everything, publish the canary schedule and send invites for the dry run. Any last blockers?
[09:36] Diego: only ask is more compute for the perf runs — I put a ticket in infra, hope it lands early tomorrow
[09:45] Maya: noted, we'll watch that ticket. Alright thanks everyone, action items in the notes, we'll reconvene Friday if any major blockers, otherwise see you at the dry run next week.
[09:57] Diego: thanks, bye
[10:00] Owen: bye
